Kim / team — attaching the preliminary artifacts listed below. These are intended to be swallowed into the HealthSys shared folder; we can tighten redaction for any customer-sensitive notes before final delivery.

Attachments included (prelim):
- vpc_topology_v2.pdf (diagram) — shows EU-WEST (Frankfurt) primary VPCs, private endpoints to model-serving subnets, and explicit peering to the customer-managed transit for the pilot.
- kms_split_diagram.png — high-level partitioning; customer data encryption keys (DEKs) and operator-wrapping keys (KEKs) are logically separated and backed by HSMs.
- keystore_operator_roster.csv — current on-call & operator list, with role (operator/read-only), jurisdiction, and last training/clearance date.
- soc2_control_extract.txt — excerpt of relevant SOC 2 control mapping for "Cryptographic Key & Key Management Controls" (control IDs and descriptions).

Short answers to the specific asks above (summary):
1) Residency: For the HealthSys pilot we will provision production resources in EU-WEST (Frankfurt) and do not enable cross-region synchronous replication. Cross-region async replication is disabled unless explicitly approved in writing and routed via private peering; no customer payload will be mirrored to non-EU regions by default. Metadata and model-choice decisions (e.g., fallback to a lower-cost US-hosted variant) may be signaled from control-plane endpoints but we do not copy customer-payload data outside the EU node.

2) Operator-keystore separation: Operator access to keystore admin paths is role-restricted and audited via our SIEM. The KEK material used to wrap DEKs is stored in HSM clusters that are logically partitioned by customer tenancy for dedicated/private runs. Access is granted via short-lived sessions and requires multi-factor operator authentication and break-glass escalation review.

3) KMS/HSM: We use an HSM-backed KMS (cloud provider HSM or customer-managed BYOK option). The diagram shows that key material for HealthSys pilot will be pinned to the EU KMS partition. Customer can opt for a customer-managed key (BYOK) if required.

4) Egress: Private endpoints and peered transit ensure that control-plane telemetry (health/checks) traverses private links. Where fallback to a US-hosted model variant could occur (for model availability), the runtime will send tokenized requests not containing PII to a compatible model endpoint; we will document the exact tokenization policy in the final pack.

Next steps: I’ll tidy the diagrams and produce a one-page attestation draft for Kimberly to sign. If Alice confirms a secure Drive link, I’ll upload the attachments there this afternoon.

Best,
Grace O’Connor
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

--- ATTACHMENT: Residency Attestation (text for PDF) ---
Redwood Inference Attestation for HealthSys Pilot (EU-WEST)
Date: 2026-09-15

Redwood Inference ("Redwood") attests that for the HealthSys pilot the following conditions will be met unless otherwise agreed in writing between Redwood and HealthSys:

1) Data Residency: Production customer payload data and persistent storage for HealthSys pilot will be hosted and stored exclusively within the EU-WEST (Frankfurt) region. Automatic cross-region replication of customer payload data is disabled by default. Any cross-border replication or persistent copying of customer payloads to regions outside EU-WEST will require explicit written approval from HealthSys and will be carried out via private peering under mutually-agreed controls.

2) Keystore & Key Management: Cryptographic key material used to encrypt HealthSys data (DEKs and KEKs) will be stored in HSM-backed partitions in the EU KMS region. Operator access to keystore administration paths is role-based, requires MFA and just-in-time session approval, and is subject to audit logging. We maintain an operator roster and recorded access reviews; keystore access logs are reviewed at least monthly and on any sensitive change events.

3) Network Isolation & Egress: Production traffic for the HealthSys pilot will traverse private endpoints and peered transit into the HealthSys environment. Control-plane metadata used for orchestration may cross regional control-plane paths, but payloads will not be transmitted outside EU-WEST absent written approval. In the event of a fallback to an alternate model variant located in another region, we will only send tokenized, non-PII request metadata unless an explicit exception is agreed.

4) Evidence & Audit References: CAIQ answers and SIG-relevant responses for network isolation and key management are included in the attached CAIQ mapping file. SOC 2 control references covering key management are included in the SOC 2 excerpt (control IDs: KM-1, KM-2).

This attestation is provided by an authorized Redwood representative for the purpose of procurement review and does not modify or supersede the terms of any executed contract.

Signed,

Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
